[[File:WTN EVula 058.jpg|thumb|The Predators have played their home games at the [[Bridgestone Arena]] (formerly the Sommet Center) since their inaugural season.]]
The [[Nashville Predators]] are an American professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Nashville, Tennessee]]. They play in the [[Central Division (NHL)|Central Division]] of the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311030113/http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 11, 2009|title=Teams|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=December 22, 2008}}</ref> The team joined the NHL in 1998 as an [[expansion team]]. The Predators have played their home games at the [[Bridgestone Arena]] since their inaugural season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://predators.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=tea_his_Timeline|title=10th Anniversary - History: Franchise Timeline|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=December 23, 2008|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080904163832/http://predators.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=tea_his_Timeline|archivedate=September 4, 2008}}</ref> The Predators are owned by Predators Holdings LLC, [[Barry Trotz]] is their [[general manager]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://predators.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=tea_stafflist|title=Team - Front Office|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=December 23, 2008|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081219180432/http://predators.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=tea_stafflist|archivedate=December 19, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://predators.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=TeamPlayers&type=roster |title=Team - Roster |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |work=NHL.com |accessdate=December 23, 2008 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090303190243/http://predators.nhl.com/team/app?service=page&page=TeamPlayers&type=roster |archivedate=March 3, 2009}}</ref>

Until the end of the 2013–14 season, the Predators franchise had only had one [[head coach]], [[Barry Trotz]]. Trotz was then replaced by [[Peter Laviolette]] on May 6, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/hockey/nhl/peter-laviolette-named-head-coach-of-predators-1.2633698|title=Peter Laviolette named head coach of Predators|publisher=CBC Sports|work=cbc.ca|accessdate=July 18, 2017}}</ref> Laviolette helped the Predators capture their first [[Clarence S. Campbell Bowl]] as well as making the team's first Stanley Cup Finals appearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nhl.nbcsports.com/2017/05/22/predators-eliminate-ducks-reach-first-stanley-cup-final-in-franchise-history/|title=Predators eliminate Ducks, reach first Stanley Cup Final in franchise history|publisher=NBC Sports|work=nbcsports.com|accessdate=July 18, 2017}}</ref>  [[John Hynes (ice hockey)|John Hynes]] replaced Laviolette during the [[2019–20 NHL season|2019–20 season]];<ref>{{cite web |title=Predators Name John Hynes Head Coach |url=https://www.nhl.com/predators/news/nashville-predators-name-john-hynes-head-coach-313572802 |website=NHL.com |access-date=January 7, 2020 |date=January 7, 2020}}</ref> after three and a half seasons, he was fired on May 30, 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Predators Relieve John Hynes of Coaching Duties, Effective Immediately |url=https://www.nhl.com/predators/news/nashville-predators-relieve-john-hynes-of-head-coaching-duties-effecti-344656716 |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 1, 2023 |date=May 30, 2023}}</ref> The following day, former Predator [[Andrew Brunette]] was named head coach.<ref>{{cite web |title=Predators Name Andrew Brunette Head Coach |url=https://www.nhl.com/predators/news/nashville-predators-name-andrew-brunette-head-coach-344661764 |website=NHL.com |access-date=June 1, 2023 |date=May 31, 2023}}</ref>
